modern:
How have you behaved up to now towards the gods, your parents, brothers, children, teachers, those who looked after you in infancy, your friends, relatives, your slaves? Consider whether you have so far behaved to all in such a way that this may be said of you:—

“Never has wronged a man in deed or word.”

And call to mind both how many things you have been through, and how many things you have been able to endure, and that the story of your life is now complete and your service is ended; and how many beautiful things you have seen; and how many pleasures and pains you have despised; and how many things called honourable you have spurned; and to how many ill-natured people you have shown kindness.
original:
How hast thou behaved hitherto to the gods, thy parents, brethren, children, teachers, to those who looked after thy infancy, to thy friends, kinsfolk, to thy slaves? Consider if thou hast hitherto behaved to all in such a way that this may be said of thee,—

“Never has wronged a man in deed or word.”

And call to recollection both how many things thou hast passed through, and how many things thou hast been able to endure, and that the history of thy life is now complete and thy service is ended; and how many beautiful things thou hast seen; and how many pleasures and pains thou hast despised; and how many things called honorable thou hast spurned; and to how many ill-minded folks thou hast shown a kind disposition.

explained.summary:
Marcus takes stock. How has he treated the gods, his parents, brothers, children, teachers, nurses, friends, relatives and slaves? Could it be said of him that he never wronged anyone in word or deed?

Then he reminds himself of all he’s been through and endured, that his story could be considered complete and his service done, and of the beauty he’s seen, the pleasures and pains he’s risen above, the honours he’s turned down and the difficult people he’s been kind to. It’s an honest audit, and also a source of quiet strength.
explained.today: At a birthday, the end of a job or late on a quiet evening, run through the people in your life: your parents, your children, your old teachers, the friend you lost touch with. Ask whether you’ve treated them well, and notice too how much you’ve already come through.
